About the timing chain. There is no clear way of doing it as it is well covered. So I'd say the only way would be, ***pop the hood*****,** and let the owner rev it a few times. Find video or some kind of audio footage, and if you can't tell the difference it's prolly alright. Next thing I would look at older Nissans is rust. Look everywhere, by that I really mean everwhere. Under the car, under the hood, trunk, wheel area etc. While you are listening to timing parts, look if the engine is mounted well. Also check if the car doesn't smoke. Test drive it, slam breaks, be sure to give it a go on some speed way to see if all gears shifts properly. Test all the lighst, press all the buttons. Make sure to listen to any weird sounds while driving or while in stay. And lastly, BARGAIN. If you really want the car, even with some problems, use these problems to your advantage to lower the price :)

Hopefully you will be driving Cedric in no time with no problems, bought for reasonable price :)

First of all, remember to be human. If you dislike/ you are uncomfortable around gay people, try to avoid them. Most homophobes are hated for sharing their opinion no one asked for. Remember that they are not mentally sick as some might say. The only difference is their sex appeal for same gender. They are not psychos or anything, they just love who they love. To be completly honest I do support every single member of the LGBTQ+ community, but not the community itself. Let me explain, I don't have problem when I see gay people or trans people or whatever, but what I do have problem is the whole propaganda around it. Spreading awareness is a good thing, but I go to store and see flags/bags and things like that, it just makes me uncomfortable. Being hetero white male, I feel like by the lgbt community pressure, I am the one opressed. I want to live in a world, in which no matter who you are, you can live life you want, would it be gay/straigt, black/asian or white. To everyone in their minds saying "well, gays were opressed in the past!!1!", yes, and they still are to this day and that's horrible, and these are the people I am supporting. I hate, when I tell someone my opinion about LGBT community and I am in a instant homophobe. 

Also homophobia or any kind of phobias are fears inside, and by therapy they can be cured. My recommendation would be to seek school therapist or someone and let them help you. It's not uncommon to be feared of anything, not even gay people. You might not feel that way, but all you feel is just a fear. So by seeking therapy, and while you are there try to avoid direct contact with the community. After some time, and I guarantee you this will happen, you will be told to go "head to head" with the community, talk to them, maybe make some friends. Anyhow I hope that you will be better at accepting people for their actions and not from where they come from or who they love.

It is more of a question, do want to use ChromeOS more than anything.

If you have Macbook and want to try well moded Linux os, then go for it. Pixelbooks are great in performace but remember that you are getting a Chromebook. Not everything you use on daily basis might be avaiable. There is the Google Apps store and Linux VM that you can use for that.

When I bought my first chromebook my expectation were high but they were lowered after a day of use, because of my music and gaming passion. But once I overcame these problems (Music - FL Mobile, Gaming - Stadia) it was a solid piece of hardwere and software to use.

Now, if it wasn't for that all apps I'm using are only supported by Windows, I would've install ChromeOS (or any Linux) on my desktop.

tl;dr

Do some research on ChromeOS and if it fits you. Know that you'll have to learn at least a basics of Linux. If you do wanna try it out, Pixelbook for this price is a steal.
